record.original_question: Which pairs of rooted polytopes have the property that their mix is itself a polytope?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Give a characterization of pairs of rooted polytopes whose mix is itself a polytope.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a partially ordered set P with a strictly monotone rank function whose elements (called faces) of ranks -1, 0, ..., n, n+1 satisfy the standard diamond and flag-connectedness conditions of an abstract n-polytope, with a unique minimum face F_{-1} and a unique maximum face F_n. A flag is a maximal totally ordered subset of P. A rooted polytope is a pair (P, Φ) consisting of an abstract polytope P together with a chosen base flag Φ.

For each rank i ∈ {0, 1, ..., n-1}, there is a unique flag Φ^i differing from Φ exactly in its rank-i face; this defines, for any P-preserving structure, distinguished involutions r_0, ..., r_{n-1} acting on the flags. The connection group (monodromy group) Mon(P) of P is the group generated by these flag-changing involutions r_0, ..., r_{n-1}.

Given two rooted polytopes (P, Φ_P) and (Q, Φ_Q) of the same rank n, with connection-group generators r_0^P, ..., r_{n-1}^P and r_0^Q, ..., r_{n-1}^Q, the mix P ◇ Q is defined as the flag system generated by the diagonal involutions s_i := (r_i^P, r_i^Q) acting on Mon(P) × Mon(Q), with base flag (Φ_P, Φ_Q). The resulting structure is always a pre-polytope, but it need not be an abstract polytope (the diamond condition or flag-connectedness can fail).

Problem: Characterize all pairs of rooted polytopes ((P, Φ_P), (Q, Φ_Q)) for which the mix P ◇ Q is itself an abstract polytope.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published characterization of when the mix of two rooted polytopes is itself an abstract polytope. The mix operation is studied in the abstract polytopes literature (e.g., the mix of a regular polytope with a face), but the general characterization problem appears to remain open, with only special cases (e.g., specific regular polytopes) treated.

status_evidence.title: The Mix of a Regular Polytope with a Face
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the mix operation in special cases involving regular polytopes and faces.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases of when the mix yields a polytope have been worked out in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Abstract Regular Polytopes (Cambridge)
status_evidence.snippet: Reference monograph on abstract polytopes including the mix of regular polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: The mix is known to be a pre-polytope; whether it is a polytope is delicate and not characterized in general.
